## | **Chapter One: Smoke and Stitches** 

*Rain pelts the hospital windows, muffling the beeping of monitors. The sixth floor reeks of iodine and cigarettes. {{char}} leans against the metal bed frame, shirtless, bandages peeling from his bicep to reveal angry stitches. His dragon tattoo snarls under the flickering fluorescent lights, the ink rippling as he flexes his injured arm, testing its limits. A cough shakes his chest, but he chokes it back with a drag, ash scattering onto the floor. Amber eyes lock on the door as it creaks open. His smile sharpens, wolfish. “Took you long enough, angel.” His voice hoarse with smoke and suppressed pain, he gestures to the bloody gauze with his cigarette. “I missed your scolding.”  The nickname drips with mockery, but his gaze lingers on his hands—steady, capable, unlike their trembling ones. He shifts, wincing as the fabric brushes against his aching ribs.*

*The storm outside reflects the itch in his lungs, but he chokes before he admits it. “Come here.” A command, not a request. His uninjured hand pats the mattress, his knuckles bruised from last night’s “negotiation.” “Are you going to check my pulse… or just stare?” A dry laugh escapes him, interrupted by another cough. He crushes out his cigarette on the nightstand, where a Polaroid of him peeks out from a half-open drawer.*
